newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Vice Premier Zhu Rongji urges people involved in grain production to purchase grain at appropriate prices.
- A conference in Beijing says government officials and members of judicial organs involved in corruption should be punished severely.
- President Jiang Zemin says Malaysian Supreme Head of State Tunku Ja'afar's visit to China will promote mutual understanding, friendship and Sino-Malaysian ties.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Chairman of National People's Congress Qiao Shi says China is willing to cooperate more closely with Thailand and members of ASEAN.
- A national conference on agriculture urges all departments in charge of agricultural production to ensure another good harvest of autumn grain.
- Premier Li Peng calls on international friends to enhance understanding and promote cooperation among Asia-Pacific nations.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Vice-Governor of the People's Bank of China Shang Fulin says active stock market affects capital liquidity and monetary policy.
- Beijing has 890,000 stock account holders by end of June.
- Shanghai Huadong Computer Co wins contract to install computer system in new headquarters of the Shanghai Commodity Exchange.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- China foreign exchange trade turnover hits $6.4 billion in June.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- Fujian province starts to build 35,000-tonne coal wharf with 220 million yuan investment.
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- China has 655 A share firms and 93 B share firms by end of June.
- The Agricultural Bank of China allocates 1.0 billion yuan for personal mortgage loans.
- Baoshan Iron and Steel Co plans to produce 8.8 million tonnes of steel in 1997.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Vice-Minister of State Economic and Trade Commission Yu Xiaosong says excessive tariff cuts will hurt domestic industry.
- Foreign colour television manufacturers slash prices to boost their market share.
- Chairman of the Chinese Olympic Committee Wei Jizhong urges sports sector to tap stock market.
- China Export-Import Bank extends loans worth $65 million to Iran and Zimbabwe.
- The Agricultural Bank of China makes loans worth 600 million yuan for state purchase of silk cocoons by end of June in 12 major producing areas.
CHINA DAILY
- China offers 80,000 tonnes of free grain to North Korea.
- Beijing to ban construction of office buildings by party and government units in the city for the next three years.
- Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang says China hopes warring factions in Cambodia will put national interests first and prevent further deterioration of the situation.
